summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to understand the case for non-stationarity of unconditional variance in stock return series, challenging standard ARCH and stochastic volatility models that assume constant unconditional variance, and the resulting proposal to locally approximate returns with stationary ARMA models on intervals of homogeneity rather than imposing global stationarity.

A researcher wants the integrated periodogram methodology used as a goodness-of-fit test in the spectral domain to delimit intervals of homogeneity in a return series, together with the weighted version of the periodogram that removes its dependence on the underlying spectral density and yields a more tractable limiting Gaussian process.

A researcher wants the theorem establishing that the weighted integrated periodogram of a linear process converges in distribution to a Kiefer-Müller process, a two-parameter Gaussian field behaving as a Brownian motion in one argument and a Brownian bridge in the other, together with the simplified form of this result for an independent white noise sequence.

summaries.field: applied financial econometrics / return time series
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to know why a return sign and size decomposition is a useful starting point for analyzing daily stock returns, given empirical evidence that the sign of returns is not predictable, motivating a focus on modeling the absolute value, or size, of returns instead.

An analyst wants a local ARMA approximation of the log-absolute return series estimated separately on each interval of homogeneity, together with the empirical finding that the fitted autoregressive and moving-average coefficients are consistently insignificant, indicating that the series behaves as white noise once the shifting mean and variance are accounted for.

An analyst wants a historical account of shifts in mean of absolute returns of a long daily stock return series, tracing periods of higher and lower volatility to major economic events, together with evidence that centering the series on this shifting mean substantially reduces the dependency present in its sample autocorrelation function.
summaries.primary_concept: shifts in mean of absolute returns
sub_concepts: shifts in mean of absolute returns

summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to know the extent of residual autocorrelation reduction achieved after centering absolute returns by their estimated shifting mean, noting that some dependency remains at short lags, together with the suggestion that a better approximation of the changing mean than a simple step function could remove this remaining dependency.

An analyst wants the stabilized-variance sub-period model for the logarithm of absolute returns, motivated by evidence that the innovation variance settled around a fixed value after the modern index structure was established, together with residual diagnostics showing that this simplified specification leaves little unexplained autocorrelation.

An analyst wants a homogeneity interval detection method comparison between the integrated periodogram goodness-of-fit test and a simpler central-limit-theorem based test statistic, together with additional evidence supporting a constant innovation variance across a later sub-period, to see which detection method offers the better overall balance of fit and simplicity.

An analyst wants a long-memory model forecasting comparison between a fractionally integrated ARIMA model and a non-stationary shifts-in-the-mean model for the logarithm of absolute returns, evaluated across many forecast horizons using a formal orthogonality test between the two forecasts, to determine which paradigm better explains the observed dependency in the return series.

An analyst wants a forecast encompassing regression designed to compare two competing forecasts of absolute returns without relying on the ergodic stationarity assumptions that the possibly non-stationary series would otherwise violate, together with the resulting test evidence favoring the shifts-in-the-mean forecast over the fractionally integrated long-memory forecast.
